grade.primary_choice: Fix in Ruby/Sidekiq first: dedicated queue and ECS service, per-endpoint isolation, Go only later if needed
unsupported_claims: The claim that the TLS handshake is 'probably most of your CPU cost today' is a guess with no data behind it
The claim that the Ruby path 'may only buy 5–10x headroom' is an estimate with no basis given
grade.notes: The answer covers every must-mention point. It uses Little's law math, isolates slow endpoints with caps, circuit breakers and a slow lane, puts webhooks on their own autoscaled ECS service, keeps the DB connection out of the HTTP call, and checks metrics before committing. It treats Go as a later escalation that weighs the on-call load on the 3-person platform team, and it handles the SaaS option with cost and data-handling caveats; the DB point says to release the connection before sending rather than pre-rendering payloads, which is close enough.
